# src/ — implementation

## Purpose
All hub and bridge code lives here on the Rust standard library only. Zero external crates is a hard constraint: every capability (crypto, JSON, HTTP, MCP) is implemented in-tree and unit-tested.

## Ownership
- `sha256.rs`, `hmac.rs`, `rand.rs` — crypto primitives. FIPS 180-4 / RFC 2104/4231 vectors are load-bearing; do not weaken or remove them.
- `keccak.rs` — FIPS 202 SHA3-256/512 + SHAKE128/256 (sponge over Keccak-f[1600]); FIPS 202 KATs load-bearing.
- `aes.rs` — FIPS 197 AES-256 block cipher; Appendix C.3 + SP 800-38A vectors load-bearing.
- `gcm.rs` — AES-256-GCM (SP 800-38D): CTR keystream + GHASH; tag compare constant-time; McGrew-Viega appendix-B vectors load-bearing. 96-bit nonces only, never reuse key+nonce.
- `ntt_tables.rs`, `mlkem768.rs` — FIPS 203 ML-KEM-768 (Kyber-derived NTT with Montgomery zetas, basemul with zetas[64±i] pairing, tomont in keygen). Official NIST ACVP KATs in `tests/vectors/` are load-bearing (keygen/encaps/decaps byte-exact). Cross-validated against pyca/cryptography and kyber-py.
- `sessions.rs` — hub-side encrypted session channel registry: members, ML-KEM-768 sealed key packages, seq-numbered ciphertext ring per session; hub stores ciphertext only and can read nothing. Fail-closed caps (sessions, members, msgs).
- `identity.rs` — bridge-side ML-KEM-768 identity keypair in `$WTF_HOME/identity.json` (0600), auto-generated on first use, corrupt file fails closed.
- `session_crypto.rs` — client-side sealing: ML-KEM-768 encapsulate of the 256-bit session key per member (AES-256-GCM wrap under SHA3-256(shared)), per-(session, sender) subkeys, AAD binds (session, sender, seq), deterministic 96-bit nonces from subkey+seq.
- `bins.rs` — shared paste-bins: three durable slots (BIN 1-3) in `bins.json` (0600) for copy-paste content handed between the human and agents, or between agents on different machines. 64 KiB per bin, rejected (never truncated) when oversize; writes persist atomically before mutating memory; agents read via `read_bin`/`list_bins` and publish via the `write_bin` MCP tool (device-signed PUT, attributed as the device name); dashboard writes keep the `dashboard` actor.
- Session channels (`sessions.rs` + `api.rs` `/api/v1/sessions*` + `mcp.rs` session tools): encrypted agent-to-agent chats. The hub stores session metadata, sealed key packages, and ciphertext in `sessions.json` (0600) — never plaintext. Creator seals the session key to each member's registered ML-KEM-768 identity; members decapsulate with `$WTF_HOME/identity.json` (0600). Message AAD binds (session, sender, seq); seq is hub-assigned monotonic per session.
- `json.rs` — strict depth-limited parser + serializer; the only JSON path for config, wire, and storage.
- `http.rs`, `client.rs` — hand-rolled HTTP/1.1. Server enforces 32 KiB head / 1 MiB body / 100 headers / 15 s timeouts; `Transfer-Encoding` requests get `501` by design.
- `auth.rs` — HMAC-SHA256 request signing (standard-crypto transport lane). Canonical string: `wtf-hmac-v1\nMETHOD\npath-and-query\nts\nnonce\nsha256hex(body)`. ±300 s skew; per-device nonce replay cache. Device lookup happens before nonce consumption so callers can reload the keystore and retry.
- `config.rs` — `$WTF_HOME` layout (default `~/.config/wtf-mcp`), atomic writes, `0600` key files, KeyStore issue/revoke/rotate, BridgeConfig with env overrides `WTF_HUB_URL` / `WTF_DEVICE_NAME` / `WTF_DEVICE_KEY`. HubConfig carries an optional `advertised_url` (set via `wtf url`) that wins over LAN auto-detection in `lan_url()`. `BridgeConfig::validate` accepts `http://` and `https://`.
- `store.rs` — `events.jsonl` is the source of truth (replayed on start, rotates at 10 MB); 1000 events in memory; generation counter drives SSE pushes.
- `api.rs` — route table + authz: `/healthz` open; `/` and `/stream` need dashboard key `?k=`; `/api/v1/state` accepts dashboard key or device auth; `/api/v1/bins` and `/api/v1/bins/{1,2,3}` (GET/PUT) accept dashboard key or device auth; `checkin`/`event`/`heartbeat`/`identity` are device-only; `/api/v1/devices` and session GET/list accept dashboard key or device; session `seal`/`seals`/`send`/`recv` are device-only and member-gated. State JSON carries `bins`; bin writes land in the event feed and bump the SSE generation. The keystore reloads from disk on every authenticated request — issue/revoke/rotate apply instantly without a hub restart; revoked devices fail closed (401).
- `dashboard.rs` — embedded single-page dark UI; no external assets; EventSource live updates.
- `mcp.rs` — stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 bridge (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping`); fourteen tools (`check_in`, `log_event`, `wtf_is_going_on`, `read_bin`, `write_bin`, `list_bins`, `ping`, `hub_info`, `session_create`, `session_list`, `session_join`, `session_seal`, `session_send`, `session_read`); application failures are `isError:true` results, never protocol errors; 60 s heartbeat thread; shared text formatter also used by `wtf status` and includes non-empty bins; `instructions` + tool descriptions mandate chain-of-draft reporting (terse fragments, <=5 words); `hub_info` answers the operator's where-is-the-hub question (URL, device, version) without ever exposing the dashboard key over MCP.
- `main.rs` — CLI: `serve`, `key issue|list|revoke` (`issue --json` emits a machine-readable enrollment line), `url` (get/set/clear advertised URL), `setup`, `join` (self-enroll by running `key issue --json` remotely over ssh; the one-time secret travels only inside the ssh channel and the remote command is charset-restricted), `agent`, `status`, `dashboard-url` (prints the operator's clickable dashboard URL; the only tooling that ever prints the dashboard key besides the serve startup line — hub machine only), `skill install|print` (distributes the embedded portable hub skill into any project's `.agents/skills/wtf-agent-hub/`; idempotent, `--force` to overwrite), `help`.

## Local Contracts
- No third-party dependencies in `Cargo.toml`, ever. Implement or do without.
- No literal IP addresses in source or docs authored by agents (tooling redacts them); build addresses from constants at runtime, use `localhost` in examples.
- Secrets (device keys, dashboard key) go only into `0600` files under `$WTF_HOME` or the one-time `wtf key issue` output; never commit or log them.
- Standard crypto for transport only. PQC (FIPS 203/204/205) is mandatory for any future secrets-at-rest feature; none exists yet.
- Bridge URLs are `http://` (trusted LAN or encrypted overlay) or `https://` (TLS-terminating proxy). The HMAC signature is the authenticity root in every topology; TLS is never implemented in-tree.
- Fail closed: unparseable input is a 4xx, auth errors never reveal which factor failed.

## Work Guidance
- Keep the HTTP parser strict; raise limits deliberately, never silently.
- A new endpoint must land in three places together: `api.rs` dispatch, the `known_path` list, and the authz model comment at the top of `api.rs`.
- Bridge tools report failures as tool results, keeping the JSON-RPC layer for protocol faults only.

## Verification
- `cargo test` — unit tests (crypto vectors incl. FIPS 202/197/203 KATs from `tests/vectors/`, GCM McGrew-Viega vectors, adversarial parser cases, auth roundtrip/tamper/replay/skew, store replay, bins persistence/rejection/fail-closed, session store caps, HTTP parse limits, advertised_url roundtrip) plus `tests/e2e.rs` (real hub + real bridge over stdio, HTTP auth negatives, bins write/read/authz/oversize incl. device-signed writes, `key issue --json` enrollment, two-agent encrypted session flow: create/join/seal/send/read with ciphertext-only hub assertions).
- `cargo build --release` must succeed (lto, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, overflow-checks).
- rustfmt/clippy are not installed in this environment; run `cargo fmt`/`cargo clippy -- -D warnings` when available.
